access.edition_or_version: Sahitya Akademi edition translated by Gordon C. Roadarmel

mechanics.premise: An impoverished Indian peasant dreams of owning a milch cow to fulfill household pride and religious duty, but is crushed by colonial-feudal debt.
mechanics.reader_promise: Unsparing, deeply empathetic portrait of rural peasant struggle against systemic exploitation by moneylenders, landlords, and caste hierarchy.
mechanics.opening: Hori prepares to take bamboo sticks to sell in town, deliberating over his mounting indebtedness and peasant dignity.
mechanics.point_of_view: Third-person omniscient realist narrative moving between rural village and urban Lucknow intellectual society.
mechanics.character_system: Hori Mahato (enduring peasant), Dhania (fierce, pragmatic wife), Gobar (rebellious son), Rai Sahib (feudal landlord), Pandit Datadin (exploitative priest).
mechanics.conflict_and_stakes: Dignity and economic survival of a rural family against systemic usury and caste sanctions.
mechanics.structure: Dual parallel plotlines contrasting village peasant reality with urban bourgeois and intellectual hypocrisies.
mechanics.scene_movement: Village courtyard, agricultural fields, panchayat hearings, Lucknow salons, sugar mill.
mechanics.dialogue: Authentic Awadhi-inflected Hindi/Urdu idioms capturing rural vernacular grit and urban affectation.
mechanics.setting: Belari village and Lucknow in 1930s colonial British India.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Social realism, tragic irony, economic materialism, symbolic weight of the sacred cow.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Persistent hope despite adversity -> mounting debt crisis -> physical exhaustion -> devastating tragic quietude.
mechanics.suspense_or_anticipation: Whether Hori's tireless labor and moral integrity can stave off total land dispossession.
mechanics.climax: Hori collapses from heatstroke while laboring on road construction to earn cash for landlord interest.
mechanics.ending: As Hori lies dying, Brahmin priest demands cow donation for his salvation; Dhania places her last 20 paise in his hand and faints.
mechanics.conventions: Masterwork of Indian social realism; refuses easy romanticization of peasant life or didactic revolutionary melodrama.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Subverts Hindu religious ritual of godan into a devastating critique of institutional exploitation at the moment of death.
mechanics.critical_reception: Widely acknowledged as the greatest modern Hindi novel and towering achievement of Indian literary realism.
mechanics.audience_reception: Profound cultural touchstone in South Asian literature and sociology.
